<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/objectql`, touching **8** documentable anchor(s).

**5** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`  _(via SchemaRegistry (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/deployment/environment-variables.mdx`  _(via SchemaRegistry (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/kernel/services-checklist.mdx`  _(via SchemaRegistry (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/plugins/adding-a-metadata-type.mdx`  _(via SchemaRegistry (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/plugin-spec.mdx`  _(via SchemaRegistry (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-4.mdx`  _(via SchemaRegistry (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **27** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 43dd5656e47001bf26ba5b441683ae836aebf816` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `caace47a5b3e4e1471b6ccef3f0bf57e0e8148dc` — the merge of head `d314ad0fb0f46447d3084a30f03e2666608aa641` into base `43dd5656e47001bf26ba5b441683ae836aebf816`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin caace47a5b3e4e1471b6ccef3f0bf57e0e8148dc && git checkout caace47a5b3e4e1471b6ccef3f0bf57e0e8148dc
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 43dd5656e47001bf26ba5b441683ae836aebf816 d314ad0fb0f46447d3084a30f03e2666608aa641 && git checkout -B drift-repro 43dd5656e47001bf26ba5b441683ae836aebf816 && git merge --no-ff d314ad0fb0f46447d3084a30f03e2666608aa641

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 43dd5656e47001bf26ba5b441683ae836aebf816
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 43dd5656e47001bf26ba5b441683ae836aebf816` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `5fb04355de18a2645b3abf7fea2e3e3db81d3602`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-registry-hydration.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-save-door-refusals.ts, packages/objectql/src/registry.ts, packages/objectql/src/protocol-permission-set-name-registry-reading.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/protocol-registry-heal-packageless-refusal.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/webhook-stored-row-boot-hydration.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/packaged-permission-set-lock.test.ts + read in the cited code, never reviewed: packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts (cold-boot call site), packages/core/src/security/security-catalog.ts (grant resolution), packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/packaged-permission-set-lock.ts (classifier), packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-package-bindings.ts (envelope merge, row binding), packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-package-lifecycle-types.ts (uninstall capture), packages/objectql/src/protocol-boot-hydration-scoped.test.ts (N.3 pins on `main`), docs/adr/0150 D2/D3/D4, skills/objectstack-data/rules/security.md

Inputs read: card #32780 body and all 6 comments; PR #34224 body, file list (8 files, +415/−55), comments; the net diff `origin/main...5fb04355de`; #34226; check-runs on the head (35 success, 16 skipped, none red, `Check Changeset`, `Test Core` 1–8/8, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, the Lint and Type Check families all success). Nothing was built or run; every statement below about `main` or the head is a code read, and says so where it contradicts a measured claim.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Save, publish, restore door, stored holder of another namespace: `422 NAMESPACE_CONFLICT` → saved.** Right, and as ordered by the card. A stored holder is judged by the one namespace predicate alone. A stored holder with no namespace, of a platform namespace, of the writer's namespace, or under a platform-requested name still meets and is still refused at this door.
- **Stored permission set bound to a package: kept per `(package, name)` in the registry**, at the write-through and at the boot hydration alike. Right for the ordered case; what follows from it for the other name checks is M1.
- **A stored set is its own package's set and wears no other package's envelope.** Right.
- **Grant resolution.** Right. A grant naming a package confers that package's set or nothing, never another holder's; a grant naming no package while two packages hold the name is refused and confers nothing. No path picks between two.
- **Lock classification.** Right. A stored set stays tenant-authored under its own package, so it neither lends the lock its package nor hides a shipped set (pinned in `packaged-permission-set-lock.test.ts`).
- **Delete of one package's stored set retires that set alone.** Right; pinned in both orders and across a restart.
- **Remedy text.** Right: a delete is offered only for a holder that stores its set, the rename otherwise; envelope unchanged.
- **Cold boot, self-bound row (Q2=B).** Right as far as it goes: the ADR-0048 N.3 pin holds.
- **Wrong: refusals `main` makes for a permission-set name are not all made on this head**, undeclared and unordered. M1.
- **Wrong: the declared FROM of the restart rows** does not match `main`'s cold boot as read. S1.
- Public surface: no exported symbol, schema, route or wire envelope moves. `registry.ts` changes one private member.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: yes (narrowing) — the arm is the right one to carry (`!`, BREAKING banner, ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`), and `patch` on `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` and `@objectstack/objectql` is the level the repo's gate reads for it (`Check Changeset` success). `plugin-security` changes a test only and needs no entry. The ADR-0087 disposition is right: no key, row shape or stored value moves, so there is nothing for a migration to rewrite.

`Metadata-protocol: none` is right: the diff touches no `packages/spec` schema, and no authorable key, value or default moves.

`Skills-docs: none` holds against `skills/objectstack-data/rules/security.md` on this head: lines 45–48 already teach naming `permission_set_package` when two packages hold the name, line 182 already says a refused name confers nothing, and no skill or docs page quotes the save door's old remedy or reason text.

What the changeset publishes is not what the tree does, in two places: the moves under M1 are undeclared and its "refusal that stays" sentence does not hold for all of them, and the FROM of the restart rows is S1. The level does not change; the two halves do.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev report 6904857828 carries `open_questions: []`. Its four deviations are answered: the `registry.ts` surface extension is the place Q2=B's reader lives and is approved by the area (6905228671); the two moved pins outside the named harness are direct consequences; importers of `objectql` left to CI are covered by the green `Test Core` shards; the claim line `yes (widening)` replaced by `yes (narrowing)` is the conservative reading.
- Report 6902631786 Q1 and Q2: the tree implements B and B. Both hold on merit — Q1=B declares more, not less, and Q2=B keeps `main`'s answer for the self-bound row. Escalated to the seat: neither ruling is a comment on card #32780; the card's six comments carry the two dev reports, a regrade and a claim, and the rulings are attested only by the dev report and the area request. N2.
- Q2's option text says the hot-install parity is "NOT MEASURED". It is still not measured on this head.
- `security_findings: withheld` in both reports: not readable here, so not judged.
- #34226 (seal and lock judge by name alone) open beside this PR: safe. The name-wide seal and lock over-refuse and never under-refuse, and no shadow, unlock or bypass of a sealed or locked set by a second namespace's stored set was found. M1 is not #34226's; a security item is with the owner seat.

### ④ Design judgment

The ordered narrowing itself is sound: a grant naming no package while two packages hold the name confers nothing, which is ADR-0150 D3's refusal made real at the consumer, not a declared capability taken away, and the remedy (`permission_set_package`) is the published one. The ordered widening is sound at the save door. The implementation is wider than both rulings.

M1 (must-fix) — after this change some security-catalog name checks no longer see a stored permission set bound to a package, so refusals `main` makes for a permission-set name are not all made on this head, undeclared and unordered. The rule owed: every door that judges who holds a permission-set name judges a stored set as its package's holding under the one namespace predicate, in either order of arrival, and a shipped set's grants are never changed by a stored row. A code read under the read-only rule, not measured. The mechanism and the owed fix are with the owner seat; a security item is with the owner seat.

S1 (should-fix) — the declared FROM of the restart rows does not match `main` as read. For "`crm` ships or declares the name, `hr` stores it, restart", `main`'s cold boot as read answers `422 NAMESPACE_CONFLICT`, not "a grant naming no package confers a set". The move at that restart is then refused → boots with each set served at its package: a widening the card orders ("every restart serves each package's set at its package"), which the PR body, the changeset and the pin comments do not state, while the declared narrowed half names a FROM a booted `main` kernel does not give. The PR's own pin "a set hr stores, then crm ships a set of the name" should be run on `main` under the same harness to settle it; the Clause-② halves, the FROM → TO table and the BREAKING sentence are then restated from what is measured. If the measurement stands against this read, the record owes the harness that shows it.

N1 (nit) — `protocol-save-door-refusals.ts`, "The holders" list: the diff turns the opening backtick of `package_id` into two. TSDoc only.

N2 (nit) — rulings Q1=B and Q2=B are not on card #32780; the seat posts them there so the declaration and the surface extension rest on a readable record. No head moves.

M1 is a FAIL; its fix and S1's restatement each earn a delta review.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `d314ad0fb0f46447d3084a30f03e2666608aa641`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-registry-hydration.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-save-door-refusals.ts, packages/objectql/src/registry.ts, packages/objectql/src/protocol-permission-set-name-registry-reading.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/protocol-registry-heal-packageless-refusal.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/webhook-stored-row-boot-hydration.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/packaged-permission-set-lock.test.ts + read in the cited code, never reviewed: packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts (cold-boot call site), packages/core/src/security/security-catalog.ts (grant resolution), packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts (the list of types stored per package), AGENTS.md step 3 (declaration and level), docs/adr/0150 D2/D3, skills/objectstack-data/rules/security.md

Delta round 1. Base record: 6905371453 at head `5fb04355de18a2645b3abf7fea2e3e3db81d3602` (FAIL: M1, S1, N1, N2).

Inputs read: `git diff 5fb04355 0e5a6203` in full (4 files, +89/−21); the merge `d314ad0f` (the PR's net diff against `main` at this head is line-for-line the one `0e5a6203` carried, 538 changed lines over the same 8 files, and what `main` brought into the two shared source files does not touch permission-set names); the PR title and body; card #32780 and its comments, with rulings 6905396672 and dev report 6906643344; the area's delta request 6907002294; the check-runs on this head (37 success, 18 skipped, none red, `Check Changeset`, `PR-body guards`, `Test Core`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, the Lint and Type Check families all success). Nothing was built or run.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Every name check counts a package's stored permission set as that package's holding of the name, under the one namespace predicate.** Right. It holds at the package door, at the item seam and at the cold boot, with the stored set arriving first or second; the save, publish and restore door already judged it from the stored rows. A holder of another namespace is admitted, a holder that meets the incoming package is refused `422 NAMESPACE_CONFLICT`, as on `main`.
- **Cold boot (ADR-0048 N.3): a stored set held against a package that declares or ships the name refuses the boot, as on `main`.** Right. That covers the declarer's own stored set, a stored set of a package that meets it under the predicate, and a stored set served as the declarer's. A stored set of a package of another namespace is that package's own and holds nothing against the declarer.
- **Restart over a stored set of one package beside a set of the name another namespace's package ships or declares: boot refused `422 NAMESPACE_CONFLICT` → boots, each set served at its package.** Right, ordered by the card ("every restart serves each package's set at its package"), and now declared.
- **Grant resolution, lock classification, delete, remedy text:** unchanged since the base record, each right as judged there.
- Public surface: no exported symbol, schema, route or wire envelope moves. The change in `registry.ts` stays in private members. The two security-catalog types other than the permission set are not stored per package, so no answer moves for them.
- The merge moved none of this PR's own hunks.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: yes (widening) — the right arm. Read against `main`'s tree, as last round: `main` refuses the cold boot in every restart state this head boots, and the area's measurement on `main`'s sources in the cold-boot harness agrees with that read. I looked for an answer that moves from accepted to refused, at each door and in each order, and found none: every name check on this head refuses a subset of what `main` refuses, and a grant naming no package of a name two packages hold conferred nothing before and confers nothing now. Two widened halves, the save door and the restart, are what the tree publishes and what the changeset, the PR body and the title now say, consistently.

Level: `patch` on `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` and `@objectstack/objectql` is right under AGENTS.md step 3 (`Metadata-protocol: none` takes `patch`; a widening is not BREAKING). Withdrawing the `!`, the BREAKING line and the ADR-0087 marker is right: the marker is owed by a breaking changeset only, and nothing here breaks. `Check Changeset` is green on this head.

`Metadata-protocol: none` stays right: no `packages/spec` schema is touched, and no authorable key, value or default moves. With no narrowing arm, no `Skills-docs:` line is owed; `skills/objectstack-data/rules/security.md` still teaches naming `permission_set_package` when two packages hold the name, and nothing it says is moved.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev report 6906643344 carries `open_questions: []`. Its two deviations: the departure from ruling Q1=B is answered on merit in ② (the premise of Q1, a measured accepted-to-refused move, does not hold on `main`'s tree); the commit trailer is not a contract matter.
- The area's delta request says the seat confirmed the restatement. That confirmation is not a comment on card #32780, where the posted ruling 6905396672 still reads Q1=B. N3.
- `security_findings: withheld`: as the rule requires; not judged here.
- #34226 open beside this PR: still safe. The name-wide seal and lock over-refuse and never under-refuse, and no shadow, unlock or bypass of a sealed or locked set by a second namespace's stored set was found on this head. One note for #34226's own fix is with the owner seat.
- The PR is still a draft; that is the area's to lift.

### ④ Design judgment

M1: closed. Every name check now counts a package's stored permission set as that package's holding, under the one namespace predicate, in both orders of arrival, and the cold boot refuses as on `main` wherever a stored set is held against a declaring or shipping package; a shipped set's grants are not changed by a stored row across a restart. Each case has its own pin (the package door and the item seam, the cold boot beside a package of the same namespace with a control of another namespace, the cold boot beside a package that ships the name, and the declarer's own stored set), and the report gives one ablation per leg, each red on exactly its pin and restored. I tried the routes of the base record again and looked for a name check the fix did not reach; I found none.

S1: closed. The declaration is restated from `main`'s measured answers and matches `main`'s tree as read: the restart rows read refused → boots, the narrowed half is gone, and the arm, level, title, body and changeset agree.

N1: closed.

N2: closed. Rulings posted as 6905396672.

No must-fix, no should-fix.

N3 (nit) — the seat's confirmation of the restated declaration is attested only by the area's delta request, while the card's posted ruling still reads Q1=B. The seat posts the confirmation on card #32780. No head moves.

N4 (nit) — one listing of the names a package holds, read when a package is uninstalled, still spells a stored set by its storage form beside the real name. The real name is still supplied from the stored rows, so nothing is missed. A follow-up card, not this head.
